title: Electric Circuits and Internal Resistance
seo_title: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Electric Circuits and Internal Resistance Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Electric circuits: internal resistance
standard_text: Internal resistance and the emf of a cell, ε = I(R + r); terminal potential difference and 'lost volts'; series–parallel networks of resistors with internal resistance; the effect of changing the external resistance; power in circuits. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Physics: Electric circuits: internal resistance)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): emf, internal resistance, terminal potential difference, series–parallel networks and power. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

A real battery has internal resistance r. When a current flows, some potential difference ('lost volts', Ir) is used inside the battery, so the terminal potential difference V = ε − Ir is less than the emf. The emf is the terminal potential difference when no current flows.

Solve series–parallel networks step by step: find the equivalent resistance of each parallel part, add the series resistances and r, then I = ε/(R + r). If the external resistance is decreased, the current increases, the lost volts increase and the terminal potential difference decreases.

Example

ε = 12 V, r = 1 Ω, R = 5 Ω. Current?

I = ε/(R + r)

Answer: 2 A

Example

Same circuit. Terminal potential difference?

V = IR

Answer: 10 V

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to add r to the external resistance.
  • Thinking the terminal p.d. always equals the emf.
  • Adding parallel resistors directly.

faq.q: Why does a car's headlights dim when the starter motor runs?
faq.a: The large current makes the lost volts (Ir) in the battery large, so the terminal p.d. drops.

faq.q: How can you find the internal resistance in an experiment?
faq.a: Plot terminal p.d. against current: the gradient of the line is −r and the y-intercept is the emf.
